overview: The School Committee approved an updated attendance policy and accepted significant grants for makerspace, cosmetology, and security. The meeting featured reports on the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility (CCSR), staffing challenges in after-school programs, and the superintendent's district goals.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Bills
items.summary: Approved minutes from the October 21 meeting and the transfer of funds for bills.

items.title: Rules Subcommittee Attendance Policy
items.summary: Approved an updated attendance policy that incorporates caregivers into the text and limits unexcused absence consequences to same-day extracurricular restrictions.

items.title: MIAA Soccer Eligibility Controversy
items.summary: High School Principal Paul D'Alleva and committee members discussed a successful legal injunction that allowed the boys' soccer team to compete after an MIAA eligibility ruling.

items.title: Superintendent's Update
items.summary: The superintendent reported on traffic closures affecting South Street bus routes, high school internet connectivity issues, and various student achievements and district grants.

items.title: CCSR Annual Report
items.summary: Accepted the annual report for the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility, which included student presentations on projects involving college mentoring, Haitian culture, and inclusive classrooms.

items.title: Student Representatives to School Committee
items.summary: Approved Mark Allen and Isabel as student representatives for the 2019-2020 school year.

items.title: Recognition of Dr. Jeanne Hollenbeck
items.summary: Recognized Dr. Jan Hollenbeck for being named to the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA) Roster of Fellows.

items.title: Donations and Security Grants
items.summary: Accepted a $10,000 Verizon grant for a high school makerspace, a $100,000 donation from the Hoff family for a cosmetology salon, and $38,502 in state funding for radio communication upgrades.

items.title: After-School Program Report
items.summary: Discussed ongoing staffing shortages and significant waitlists at elementary sites. The committee ordered a full financial report on the program and a cost-benefit analysis for moving to universal enrollment.

items.title: Math Learning Walks
items.summary: Reviewed a report and video presentation detailing district-wide instructional observations focused on mathematics standards.

items.title: Superintendent's Goals
items.summary: Approved the superintendent's 2019-2020 goals, which maintain an aggressive target for 10% growth in elementary math MCAS performance.

items.title: New Business and Executive Session
items.summary: Passed resolutions of condolence and voted to enter executive session to discuss legal matters.
